note: GASActionBuffer::Execute, opcode 0x52 ActionCallMethod: the method name is popped as a VALUE and only then coerced, so an *undefined* name (not the string "undefined") means the object on the stack is itself the function. That is how the AS2 compiler emits super(...), so before this not one class constructor in the cook ran past its first statement

GASActionBuffer::Execute, opcode 0x53 ActionNewMethod: the same blank-name rule, and both `new` opcodes now resolve a constructor held as an object through ToFunction and log the name when they cannot

InvokeContext::Setup: a super(...) call carries the GASSuperObject as its `this`; the body sees pRealThis but the NEXT super is derived from the super object's own prototype. Deriving it from the unwrapped instance made every class hierarchy recurse on itself - 609 stack overflows in one six-frame run of the main menu

GASExecutionContext::ExtendsOpCode: the SUPERCLASS is Top(0) and the subclass Top(1). This tree had them the other way round, so all 45 __Packages classes of the main menu replaced their BASE class's prototype - and the six that extend MovieClip directly overwrote MovieClip.prototype, which is where attachMovie, getNextHighestDepth and gfx.motion.Tween's mixin live

GASEnvironment::LocalRegisterPtr: the DefineFunction2 register window is the TAIL of the array and is indexed BACKWARDS - &Registers[Count - i - 1]. Indexing from the front gave every nested call the same register slots as its caller, so a constructor's `this` was overwritten by the callee's `super` between two statements

GASEnvironment::SetVariable: a dotted path is resolved to a VALUE and the member set on its object interface, so a prefix naming an ordinary object works. Walking it with FindTarget, which only follows characters, stopped at `_root.texts` - the object InitTexts creates - so all 149 localised strings of the main menu were written to nothing
GASEnvironment::GetVariable: the same rule on the read side

GFxSprite::ExecuteImportedInitActions: an imported movie's init actions run in the importing sprite. Reconstructed as a GASImportInitActionsTag the ImportAssets loader leaves in the frame's init-action list, which is the shape GFxInitImportActions has (0xa1c790 / ExecuteInContext 0xa1bd10). Without it the five screens the main menu imports from OptionsMenu.swf and LoadGame.swf arrived with their artwork and without their classes

GFxSprite::GetMember: a named child of the display list is a member of its parent. Already present in GFxSprite::GetMemberRaw; the base GFxASCharacter::GetMemberRaw now answers it too, before the prototype chain

GFxSprite::AttachMovie: the clip's own first frame runs BEFORE its class constructor, because the constructor reads the children that frame places (_common.GenericMenu's does). The timeline path already had this order

GFx_ImportLoader: also records the resolved source movie per import and leaves the init-action tag above; GetExportedName and GetExportedId fall back to the import table, because an imported character is exported by the movie it came from

GASStringManager::~GASStringManager: a node something still holds is leaked rather than freed. The action buffers of a movie DEFINITION keep their constant pool as GASStrings and the loader outlives the movie root, so freeing them made every such reference a read of freed memory at shutdown

setInterval / setTimeout / clearInterval: a timer list on the movie root, serviced at the head of Advance next to ProcessInput. They were stubs that returned a handle and did nothing, and the main menu sequences its whole opening animation with them - the logo, the blades, the splatters and the menu bar each start from one

FGFxExternalInterface::Callback: the AS2 half, flash.external.ExternalInterface.call, and GFxMovieRoot::SetExternalInterfaceRetVal, which is how the callback answers. The main menu asks the game req_CanContinueGame / req_CanLoadGame / req_CanStartNewGame / req_IsSaveLoadEnabled through it
FGFxFSCommandHandler::Callback: the AS2 half. ActionGetURL/GetURL2 split on the "FSCommand:" prefix and call the handler; every menu transition in Dishonored is one of these

FGFxRenderer::SetMatrix: the matrix is COPIED into a render command that writes CurrentMatrix when it executes (FGFxRendererImpl::SetUITransformMatrix<GMatrix2D> 0x5c6750, command Execute 0x5b8d00). As a plain game-thread store every draw of a frame was placed with the LAST transform the frame set: the DISHONORED logo was drawn at the vignette corner's position and size, and the vignette's pieces were smeared over the frame

FGFxRenderer::SetCxform: the same command (SetUITransformMatrix<Cxform> 0x5bd9e0). A game-thread mirror is kept for FillStyleColor and FillStyleBitmap, which capture the colour transform when they ENQUEUE

UDisGFxMoviePlayerBase::PreLoad: the two calls this tree was missing after the base call - SetVariable("_global.PlatformName", L"PC") and UpdateGamepadUseForAS. The start screen branches on PlatformName to choose t_PressAnyKey over t_PressStart, so its field read `undefined`
UDisGFxMoviePlayerBase::UpdateGamepadUseForAS: sets _global.bUsingGamepad, the mouse cursor count and calls _root.UIBase.UpdateControllerButtonsInstances

GFxShapeCharacterDef::Display: a style group whose image fill has no texture is not submitted at all. The renderer keeps the last fill it was given, so drawing it anyway paints the previous shape's bitmap over this one's area
the display walk: a subtree whose composed colour transform multiplies alpha by zero is not submitted. The main menu keeps two whole imported SCREENS on its display list at _alpha 0

GFxDisplayContext: carries the movie data def a shape's fill ids index, which is the movie the shape was parsed out of and not the root's - the same distinction GFxSprite::GetOwnDataDef keeps for PlaceObject
ActionTrace reaches the host log rather than stdout; the game has no console and the content's own trace() is the only narration its classes give

GASObject::GetMemberRaw: the builtin name the body special-cases at string-context +336 is __resolve, not __constructor__. The exe's own builtin table settles it - 0xdb6234 "__resolve", 0xdb6240 "_listeners", 0xdb624c "__constructor__", 0xdb625c "constructor", 0xdb6268 "__proto__" - so +320 and +336 are __proto__ and __resolve, four entries apart. Reading it as __constructor__ turned every read of an ABSENT member into a PROPERTY whose getter was the object's own constructor, and the interpreter ran it: _common.SelectionHandler reads this._bRightClick, which the menu bar never sets, so the handler re-entered its own constructor inside its own element loop, wiped _elementID and _targetMc, and every button after the first was looked up under the member name "NaN"

GASEnvironment::OperatorNew: the instance is made by the constructor's own CreateNewObject (the vtable slot at +60; the body names it in its error string), and the constructor asked is the one the PROTOTYPE's __constructor__ holds, not always the one the opcode named. Without it `new Array()` was a plain object wearing Array.prototype: push found no element store and length was not a member, so MainMenuButtonBar::SetMenu handed GenericMenu::SetMenu an array whose length was undefined and the bar was built with no entries at all

GFxASCharacter::SetStandardMember cases 2, 3, 8, 9 and 10: _xscale, _yscale, _width, _height and _rotation can be WRITTEN. This tree answered only _x, _y, _alpha and _visible and let the rest fall through to the member store, where they changed nothing - so MainMenuButton::SetText's `_upLine_mc._width = txt._width + 50` and the roll-over's `_xscale = 250` were both lost and every button kept the authored art's 244-pixel extent

GFxEditTextCharacter::GetBounds: a text field's extent is its document view's rect through the matrix, and GFxTextDocView::GetViewRect (0xa9f2c0) formats first when the view is dirty. With no override the field reported its DEFINITION's rect, which is empty for every field the cook creates from a library symbol, so `txt.autoSize = true; txt._width` answered 0

GFxEditTextCharacter::GetInitialFormats: the definition's font id is resolved against the movie that owns the field. MainMenu's DefineEditText carries font 31 or 53 and its ImportAssets2 binds those to $NormalFont and $TitleFont in gfxfontlib; the resolution is done in GFxEditTextCharacterDef::CreateCharacterInstance (0xa32df0), the only step that has the movie. The stand-in was "the first font the process registered", so every label in the game drew in the wrong face - PRESS ANY KEY measured 0.074 of the frame's width against the reference's 0.126, at the same height

UDisGFxMoviePlayerMenuBase::Req_CanContinueGame and Req_CanSaveGame: the two of the four the main menu bar asks through ExternalInterface that had no body. Continue answers !engine || HasSaveGame(0), which is what retail's UDisGFxMoviePlayerMainMenu::PostStart (2012 0x821e00) computes for the same question; Save answers the engine's m_bSaveLoadEnabled (0x62bb50). Both were DISHONORED_NATIVE_STUB bodies in the generated stub file

GFxASCharacter::GeomData (GetGeomData 0x9ceb10, SetGeomData 0x9cf3b0, EnsureGeomDataCreated 0x9cf410, MatrixScaleAndRotate2x2 0x9cdf10): the five geometry properties AS2 can write are kept beside the matrix they were last consistent with, and every setter re-derives from THAT matrix. Without it `_width = w` compounded on the previous write and a clip with a rotation was sized along the screen axes instead of its own - the menu bar is written twice per button and its 1.9 degree skew is the other half of the same arithmetic

GFxMovieDefImpl::GetExportedResource: this movie's own exports first, then recursively every movie it imports, skipping the caller so a cycle terminates. GFxSprite::AttachMovie resolved only the movie's own export table, so the DLC row's icon (lib_X_Multi, exported by ../common_assets/lib.swf and not named in MainMenu's ImportAssets2) never attached and the row's whole content went to NaN on `btn._x = btn._width / 2`

GFxTextParagraph::SetTextFormat: each run the range covers gets `existing.Merge(f)`, so only the fields the incoming format marks present override. Interning the incoming format as-is wiped the font handle and the size off every run, and the one line of the main menu that sets textColor - the DLC row - laid its 29 glyphs out and then drew none of them

FGFxRenderTargetResource::InitDynamicRHI: the UI's target now allocates a depth-stencil surface of its own. Retail takes the scene's (OwnerDepth->GetDepthTargetSurface()) and that seam is not reachable from GFxUI yet; with NO depth-stencil bound D3D9 drops every stencil operation, so the six mask passes the menu bar submits had no effect and each button's highlight drew at the full width of its artwork

GFxGlyphRasterCache::GetGlyph: the census's "missed" is the CACHE-miss count - one per distinct glyph by construction, so it can never be zero while text is drawn. The census now reports packed / blank / failed, and failed is what a defect would show in
